advisory_headline.tr: Butan dünyanın en huzurlu ve en güvenli krallıklarındandır; seyahat için önceden vize ve Sürdürülebilir Kalkınma Ücreti (SDF) şarttır.
advisory_headline.en: Bhutan is exceptionally peaceful and safe; travelers must obtain an electronic visa and pay the Sustainable Development Fee (SDF).
advisory_headline.de: Bhutan ist eines der sichersten und friedlichsten Reiseländer der Erde; Visum und Nachhaltigkeitsgebühr (SDF) erforderlich.
advisory_headline.ru: Бутан — исключительно мирное и безопасное королевство; требуется оформление визы и уплата туристического сбора SDF.
advisory_headline.es: Bután es uno de los reinos más seguros y pacíficos del mundo; requiere visa previa y Tasa de Desarrollo Sostenible (SDF).

mobile_down_mbps.evidence_quote: Median mobile broadband download speeds in Bhutan reach approximately 30.0 Mbps

fixed_down_mbps.evidence_quote: Median fixed broadband download speeds in Thimphu measure 42.0 Mbps

esim_sim_notes.value: B-Mobile (Bhutan Telecom) and TashiCell provide tourist 4G SIMs at Paro International Airport (PBH). The daily Sustainable Development Fee (SDF) of US$100 per person per night supports free healthcare, education, and carbon-negative forestry.
esim_sim_notes.evidence_quote: SDF levy of US$100 per adult per night is mandatory for all international visitors entering Bhutan

religion.value: Vajrayana Buddhism (approx. 75% official religion) and Hinduism (approx. 22%)
religion.evidence_quote: Vajrayana Buddhism permeates national governance, philosophy of Gross National Happiness (GNH), and art

festivals.value: Paro Tshechu (sacred cham masked dances), Thimphu Tshechu, Punakha Drubchen, Black-Necked Crane Festival in Phobjikha
festivals.evidence_quote: Tshechu festivals feature monks in elaborate silk brocade masks performing spiritual Cham dances

legal_cultural_warnings.value: Strict dress code inside Dzongs (fortress-monasteries): long sleeves, long trousers/skirts, and collared shirts are mandatory. Photography is prohibited inside temple sanctums. Commercial sale of tobacco products is banned by law. Bhutan is the world's first carbon-negative country.
legal_cultural_warnings.evidence_quote: Modest attire with full-length sleeves and trousers is strictly enforced in religious dzongs

tipping.value: Tipping is not traditional in Bhutanese daily life, but tipping dedicated tour guides and drivers ($10-15 per day for guide, $8-10 for driver) is standard for guided itineraries.
tipping.evidence_quote: Tipping guides and drivers at the conclusion of cultural tours is customary
